desc:
Invoice processing into your accounting tool reads supplier invoices from your inbox and creates draft bills for a person to approve. Ecom Swift LLC sets up the capture flow so nothing is posted or paid without a human review.

## What is invoice processing?

Invoice processing is the path a supplier invoice takes from arrival to your accounting software. The flow opens the PDF, captures the supplier, invoice number, date, tax and totals, and creates a draft bill in a tool such as Xero, QuickBooks or Wave. A draft is only a proposal. A person looks at it, corrects anything that is wrong and approves it.

That is what separates this from automatic payment. The flow saves the typing, and your team keeps the decisions.

## Why manual invoice entry is a weak point

Supplier invoices arrive at all hours, in many layouts, often as email attachments. Someone has to open each one, find the right figures and type them into the books. When that person is away or busy, bills wait and late payment fees can follow. When they are rushed, a total is transposed or the same invoice is entered twice.

Month-end makes it worse. A heap of unentered invoices turns reporting into guesswork, and the books say little about what you owe until the pile is cleared.

## How capture changes your cash visibility and workload

When invoices become draft bills on arrival, your books reflect what you owe much sooner. You see upcoming payments earlier and can plan cash around them. Your bookkeeper starts from a ready draft instead of an empty form, and spends their time on checking and coding rather than typing.

A duplicate check helps avoid paying the same bill twice. Matching to purchase order numbers shows when a supplier bills for something you did not order. An exceptions list gathers the invoices that the flow could not read confidently, so effort goes to the few that need it. How much time you save depends on invoice volume and how varied your suppliers' layouts are.

## What a good invoice flow includes

- Reading from one dedicated email address, so invoices are easy to separate from other mail.
- Capture of supplier name, invoice number, issue date, due date, tax and totals.
- Line items captured where your accounting setup needs them.
- Draft bills created in your accounting tool, never posted or paid automatically.
- A duplicate check on supplier and invoice number.
- Matching to your purchase order numbers, where you use them.
- An approval step by email or chat before a draft is finalized.
- An exceptions list for unclear invoices and new layouts.
- The original PDF attached to each draft for easy checking.
- Handover notes that explain how each part works.

## How we build it

First we study a batch of your real invoices from different suppliers. Each layout is tested, and we record which fields read cleanly and which need help. We then connect the inbox and your accounting software, using the connection method that tool offers.

We run the flow on past invoices, compare the drafts with what your books show and fix every mismatch. For the Basic package, results are saved to one import-ready sheet. Standard creates drafts directly in your accounting tool, with line items, tax and a duplicate check. Premium covers many more supplier layouts, purchase order matching, an approval step, an exceptions list and a test month of live runs with handover notes.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Ask suppliers to send invoices to one dedicated address.
- Keep chart of accounts and tax codes tidy, so drafts are coded sensibly.
- Review every draft before approval, at least at first.
- Check the exceptions list each day.
- Tell us when a supplier changes layout.

**Avoid:**
- Turning on automatic posting before the drafts have proved reliable.
- Mixing invoices with general mail in the same inbox.
- Ignoring duplicate warnings.
- Using the flow for statements, quotes and credit notes without testing them.
- Skipping the match to purchase orders when you rely on them.

## Who this service is for

It suits a small business with a bookkeeper who spends days each month typing supplier bills. It suits an accountant managing several clients, each with a modest but steady stream of invoices. It also suits a growing company that needs to know sooner what it owes without hiring another data entry role.

## What we need from you

We need a sample of recent invoices from your regular suppliers, the accounting tool you use and the email address where invoices arrive. Tell us who approves bills. We never ask for passwords. The accounting connection is made through the tool's own permission screen, or through a user invited with limited rights, and you can end that access at any time.
